speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. She is currently on oral isotretinoin and an oral contraceptive.

speaker: Doctor
text:

Do you have any personal or family history of similar symptoms, and have you had any recent imaging or blood tests to evaluate your adrenal or ovarian function?

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of congenital virilization (labial fusion, clitoromegaly), primary amenorrhea, severe acne, and bone fragility is highly suggestive of a congenital adrenal hyperplasia variant, likely 11-beta-hydroxylase or 17-alpha-hydroxylase deficiency, or a rare form of CAH with significant androgen excess leading to premature epiphyseal closure and osteoporosis.

REQUEST TEST: Karyotype, Pelvic_Ultrasound, Adrenal_CT
REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic Ultrasound: Ovaries with multiple cysts and a normal uterus.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound showing a normal uterus and ovaries with multiple cysts helps rule out androgen insensitivity syndrome and Mullerian agenesis, keeping the focus on CAH.

REQUEST TEST: Serum_Cortisol, Plasma_Renin, Plasma_Aldosterone, 11-deoxycortisol
REQUEST TEST: Serum_LH, FSH

speaker: Doctor
text:
The normal renin and aldosterone levels effectively rule out 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency, which typically presents with hypertension and suppressed renin. Given the severe virilization, bone fragility from androgen excess, and normal electrolytes, this clinical picture is classic for 21-hydroxylase deficiency, the most common form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)
